findings_and_reconciliations.title: Merchant gold preview nets distinct buy and sell operations and applies first sale-row price
findings_and_reconciliations.trace: The script keys buys by catalog item and sales by inventory row, preserves separate lists on submission, yet preview first nets quantities by catalog item and chooses one buy price or the first matching sale-row price. A sale then same-item buy leaves both maps populated; one each yields net zero despite reducer computing separate purchase cost and row-specific proceeds. Template quotes buy and sale separately. For a food lot, template sell price is calculated from the lot total and server quotes the complete lot once, while the preview multiplies that lot quote by the number of units in the staged row. Same-item rows can have separately computed food lot prices, yet the preview uses the first row price for all net sales.
findings_and_reconciliations.conditions: For spread: eligible stocked item and owned sale row in the same scope, successful sale-then-buy staging, non-equal valid buy and sell quotes, and successful reducer admission. For food-lot multiplication: valid sellable complete lot quantity n>1 with nonzero quoted price and matched quote context. For multi-row first-price issue: at least two accepted same-item sale rows with distinct prices. The source-only centered-dialog CSS did not reveal a full-screen backdrop in these bounded rules, but real user interaction, actual stock/data, full navigation/focus routing, currency rounding, successful transaction and UI display remain unverified. No unauthorized mutation or runtime witness is claimed.
findings_and_reconciliations.future_repair_direction: Reconcile the staged operation model and preview with authoritative separately priced buy and exact sale rows, including whole-lot and nested/measured terms; retain reducer authority, explicit quote freshness, stock and validation checks. Decide timing of any later product verification separately.
relationships: 059 q549 already recorded the price netting/first-sale question as conditional and sought the native producer and reducer. This extends that question rather than inventing a different historical finding. The reset/provisioning concerns within q549 remain separately open.

Transfer modes one/target/all and boolean-like replace_occupied are carried through DOM and forms; changing representation requires tracing native producer and admission, not turning every native boolean/string into a bespoke type.

Native u64 inventory identity and checked target quantity have existing owners; JS Number attachment path loses exactness under stated condition. Existing native merchant operation values and rows should remain authoritative.

Price netting, multiplication and first-price selection combine independently priced rows; q549. Checked reducer totals and atomic row validation remain separate from preview; no arithmetic execution.

u32 maximum and JS safe integer checks have explicit boundary roles; 999 is present as UI stock quantity while provisioning can stage more, but finite-stock policy and native stock meaning are unresolved.

Dataset values and comma-separated form fields are native encodings; current template passes catalog item ID to item-name attribute and CSS.escape is used for merchant selectors. No delimiter injection or prose identity defect asserted without full catalog/receiver proof.

DOM controls feed JS retained maps, separate form fields and native request/reducer. Replacement/identity requires coordinated producer and checked receiver migration; old/historical support stays separately attributed.

Target DOM is updated ahead of server acknowledgment and price preview recalculates state that reducer quotes independently. Resolve authority/quote freshness policy; user display cannot become independent durable authority.

Inventory row identity differs from catalog item identity and lot total differs from unit price. Equipment parent ID, placement index and human icon label serve distinct roles; do not merge them based on common underlying primitive.

InventoryItem owns primary ID, request/reducer owns native transaction validation and equipment graph owns displacement; JS draft owns transient presentation. Exact cross-family repair grouping and canonical owner decisions remain for central reconciliation.
